title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: OCR scanning of images on Windows devices (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: Windows file path exclusions can be configured with Security & Compliance PowerShell, contrary to the table's claim that automation is not documented. The roadmap facts and the documented OCR controls, billing requirements and limits are otherwise supported, with government-cloud availability and billing appropriately left unconfirmed.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans OCR detection of sensitive content in images on Windows endpoint devices.
claims.quote: Optical character recognition (OCR) support will detect sensitive content in images

claims.claim: The planned detection applies DLP policies to prevent sensitive data leaving Windows endpoints.
claims.quote: subsequently apply data loss prevention (DLP) policies to prevent exfiltration of that sensitive data on your Windows endpoint devices.

claims.claim: The release description supports JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP and image-only PDF files.
claims.quote: This release supports key file types like JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP and PDF (image only PDF).

claims.claim: OCR applies existing DLP policies to images as well as text-based content.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-policies#policy-settings, which says 'Microsoft Purview includes OCR (preview) settings' for DLP and related solutions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Purview OCR overview counts each scanned stand-alone image as one transaction.
claims.quote: Each image scanned counts as one transaction. This pricing means that stand-alone images (JPEG, JPG, PNG, BMP, or TIFF) each count as a single transaction.
claims.fix: Add after the image-transaction sentence: 'The document-processing pricing page instead describes TIF and TIFF usage per page and says processing occurs each time a file is edited; its wording differs from the Purview overview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/documentprocessing/syntex-pay-as-you-go-services, which states 'the number of pages processed for PDF, TIF, or TIFF' and 'Processing occurs every time the file is edited.'

claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api with kind 'powershell', call 'Set-PolicyConfig -EndpointDlpGlobalSettings @(@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="<folder>"})', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-policyconfig?view=exchange-ps'; update its rendered automation cell and cite that reference. Replace the final automation-absence sentence with: 'At the time of writing (November 2026), Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell cmdlet, Microsoft Graph or other API for tenant OCR settings or the Endpoint DLP bandwidth limit. Windows file path exclusions can be configured in Security & Compliance PowerShell with Set-PolicyConfig -EndpointDlpGlobalSettings using Setting="PathExclusion" and Value for the folder path; the Graph ocrSettings resource applies to an eDiscovery case.'
